cat("\n=== Model Performance Comparison Table ===\n\n")

kable(comparison_results, 
      caption = "Performance Comparison: Qualitative vs Quantitative vs ML Approaches",
      col.names = c("Approach", 
                    "PFS C-Index", "PFS Log-Rank P", "PFS N", "PFS AIC",
                    "OS C-Index", "OS Log-Rank P", "OS N", "OS AIC")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  add_footnote(c("C-Index: Harrell's concordance index (higher is better, 0.5 = random, 1.0 = perfect)",
                 "Log-Rank P: P-value from log-rank test (lower is better)",
                 "AIC: Akaike Information Criterion (lower is better)",
                 "N: Number of patients included in analysis"), 
               notation = "symbol")

# Display C-index comparison table
if (exists("c_index_comparison_os")) {
  cat("\n=== C-Index Comparison Table (OS) ===\n\n")
  kable(c_index_comparison_os,
        caption = "Statistical Comparison of OS C-Indices: Quantitative vs Other Approaches",
        col.names = c("Comparison", "Approach 1 C-Index", "Approach 2 C-Index", 
                     "Difference", "P-Value", "N (Common Patients)")) %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
    add_footnote(c("P-value from bootstrap test (n=1000) comparing C-indices",
                   "Difference = Approach 1 C-Index - Approach 2 C-Index",
                   "P < 0.05 indicates statistically significant difference in discrimination ability"),
                 notation = "symbol")
  cat("\n\n")
}

cat("\n\n=== How to Interpret the Results ===\n\n")

cat("**1. C-Index (Concordance Index)** - Discrimination Ability:\n")
cat("   - Range: 0.5 (random) to 1.0 (perfect)\n")
cat("   - > 0.6 = Good discrimination\n")
cat("   - > 0.7 = Excellent discrimination\n")
cat("   - > 0.8 = Outstanding discrimination\n")
cat("   - Higher is ALWAYS better\n\n")

cat("**2. Log-Rank P-value** - Statistical Significance:\n")
cat("   - Tests if survival curves differ significantly between groups\n")
cat("   - P < 0.05 = Significant differences (groups are meaningfully different)\n")
cat("   - P = 0 (or < 0.001) = Highly significant\n")
cat("   - All three approaches show P = 0, meaning all successfully stratify patients\n\n")

cat("**3. AIC (Akaike Information Criterion)** - Model Fit:\n")
cat("   - Lower is better (penalizes model complexity)\n")
cat("   - Difference of 2-3 points = Meaningful difference\n")
cat("   - Difference of >10 points = Substantial difference\n")
cat("   - Used to compare models: Lower AIC = Better fit for complexity\n\n")

cat("**4. N (Sample Size)** - Robustness:\n")
cat("   - More patients = More robust/stable results\n")
cat("   - Consider when comparing approaches with different sample sizes\n\n")

cat("**Interpreting Your Results:**\n\n")

# Calculate which is best for each metric
if (exists("comparison_results")) {
  # PFS Analysis
  best_pfs_c <- comparison_results$Approach[which.max(comparison_results$PFS_C_Index)]
  best_pfs_aic <- comparison_results$Approach[which.min(comparison_results$PFS_AIC)]
  
  cat("**For PFS (Progression-Free Survival):**\n")
  cat("  - Best Discrimination (C-Index):", best_pfs_c, 
      "(C-Index =", max(comparison_results$PFS_C_Index, na.rm = TRUE), ")\n")
  cat("  - Best Model Fit (AIC):", best_pfs_aic, 
      "(AIC =", min(comparison_results$PFS_AIC, na.rm = TRUE), ")\n")
  
  # Determine overall best for PFS
  if (best_pfs_c == best_pfs_aic) {
    cat("  → Overall Best for PFS:", best_pfs_c, "\n")
    cat("    (Best in both discrimination AND model fit)\n")
  } else {
    cat("  → Trade-off: Higher discrimination (", best_pfs_c, 
        ") vs Better fit (", best_pfs_aic, ")\n")
    cat("    Recommendation: Prioritize C-Index for clinical utility\n")
  }
  cat("\n")
  
  # OS Analysis
  best_os_c <- comparison_results$Approach[which.max(comparison_results$OS_C_Index)]
  best_os_aic <- comparison_results$Approach[which.min(comparison_results$OS_AIC)]
  
  cat("**For OS (Overall Survival):**\n")
  cat("  - Best Discrimination (C-Index):", best_os_c, 
      "(C-Index =", max(comparison_results$OS_C_Index, na.rm = TRUE), ")\n")
  cat("  - Best Model Fit (AIC):", best_os_c, 
      "(AIC =", min(comparison_results$OS_AIC, na.rm = TRUE), ")\n")
  
  if (best_os_c == best_os_aic) {
    cat("  → Overall Best for OS:", best_os_c, "\n")
    cat("    (Best in both discrimination AND model fit)\n")
  } else {
    cat("  → Trade-off: Higher discrimination (", best_os_c, 
        ") vs Better fit (", best_os_aic, ")\n")
    cat("    Recommendation: Prioritize C-Index for clinical utility\n")
  }
  cat("\n")
  
  cat("**Key Differences Between Approaches:**\n\n")
  
  # Calculate differences
  pfs_c_diff <- max(comparison_results$PFS_C_Index, na.rm = TRUE) - min(comparison_results$PFS_C_Index, na.rm = TRUE)
  os_c_diff <- max(comparison_results$OS_C_Index, na.rm = TRUE) - min(comparison_results$OS_C_Index, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  cat("  - PFS C-Index range:", round(pfs_c_diff, 3), 
      "(difference between best and worst)\n")
  if (pfs_c_diff > 0.05) {
    cat("    → Substantial difference in discrimination ability\n")
  } else if (pfs_c_diff > 0.02) {
    cat("    → Moderate difference in discrimination ability\n")
  } else {
    cat("    → Small difference - approaches perform similarly\n")
  }
  
  cat("  - OS C-Index range:", round(os_c_diff, 3), 
      "(difference between best and worst)\n")
  if (os_c_diff > 0.05) {
    cat("    → Substantial difference in discrimination ability\n")
  } else if (os_c_diff > 0.02) {
    cat("    → Moderate difference in discrimination ability\n")
  } else {
    cat("    → Small difference - approaches perform similarly\n")
  }
  cat("\n")
  
  cat("**Clinical Recommendation:**\n")
  cat("  - For clinical decision-making, prioritize C-Index (discrimination)\n")
  cat("  - C-Index directly measures how well the model separates high-risk from low-risk patients\n")
  cat("  - AIC is useful for model selection but less directly relevant to clinical utility\n")
  cat("  - All approaches show significant stratification (P = 0), so all are statistically valid\n")
  cat("  - Choose the approach with highest C-Index for the outcome of interest\n\n")
}
```

```{r ml_model_formula, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
# ==============================
# ML Model Formula for Clinical Use
# REMOVED: Not needed for current analysis
# ==============================

cat("\n=== ML Model Formula for Clinical Application ===\n\n")

if (exists("ml_model_parameters") && exists("cluster_names")) {
  
  cat("**HOW TO CALCULATE PATIENT GROUPING USING THE ML MODEL**\n\n")
  
  cat("**Step 1: Calculate Features for Your Patient**\n\n")
  cat("For each patient, calculate the following features from their ctDNA measurements:\n\n")
  
  # Create feature descriptions mapping
  feature_desc_map <- c(
    "n_measurements" = "Total number of ctDNA measurements",
    "mean_ctdna" = "Mean ctDNA value across all measurements",
    "median_ctdna" = "Median ctDNA value",
    "max_ctdna" = "Maximum ctDNA value observed",
    "min_ctdna" = "Minimum ctDNA value observed",
    "sd_ctdna" = "Standard deviation of ctDNA values",
    "n_positive" = "Number of positive ctDNA measurements (>0)",
    "n_negative" = "Number of negative ctDNA measurements (=0)",
    "became_negative" = "1 if patient had positive baseline and later became negative, else 0",
    "became_positive" = "1 if patient had negative baseline and later became positive, else 0",
    "last_value" = "Last ctDNA measurement value",
    "first_value" = "First ctDNA measurement value",
    "pct_change_baseline" = "Percent change from baseline to last: ((last - baseline)/baseline)*100 (or 100 if baseline=0 and last>0)",
    "time_span_days" = "Number of days between first and last ctDNA measurement",
    "trend" = "Linear regression slope of ctDNA values over time (from first to last measurement)",
    "cv_ctdna" = "Coefficient of variation: sd/mean (0 if mean=0)",
    "trend_per_day" = "Trend normalized by time span: trend/time_span_days",
    "clearance_pattern" = "1 if baseline>0 and became negative, else 0",
    "conversion_pattern" = "1 if baseline=0 and became positive, else 0",
    "persistent_positive" = "1 if baseline>0, never became negative, and last>0, else 0",
    "persistent_negative" = "1 if baseline=0, never became positive, and last=0, else 0"
  )
  
  feature_descriptions <- tibble(
    Feature = ml_model_parameters$feature_cols,
    Description = ifelse(ml_model_parameters$feature_cols %in% names(feature_desc_map),
                        feature_desc_map[ml_model_parameters$feature_cols],
                        ml_model_parameters$feature_cols)
  )
  
  kable(feature_descriptions, 
        caption = "Features Required for ML Model Classification",
        col.names = c("Feature Name", "How to Calculate")) %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
  
  cat("\n\n**Step 2: Scale Features Using Training Set Parameters**\n\n")
  cat("For each feature, apply the following transformation:\n\n")
  cat("```\n")
  cat("scaled_feature = (raw_feature - center) / scale\n")
  cat("```\n\n")
  cat("Where 'center' and 'scale' are the training set mean and standard deviation:\n\n")
  
  # Create scaling parameters table
  scaling_params <- tibble(
    Feature = names(ml_model_parameters$scale_center),
    Center = round(ml_model_parameters$scale_center, 4),
    Scale = round(ml_model_parameters$scale_scale, 4)
  )
  
  kable(scaling_params, 
        caption = "Scaling Parameters (Training Set Statistics)",
        col.names = c("Feature", "Center (Mean)", "Scale (SD)")) %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
    scroll_box(width = "100%", height = "400px")
  
  cat("\n\n**Step 3: Calculate Distance to Each Cluster Center**\n\n")
  cat("For each cluster (1 to ", ml_model_parameters$n_clusters, "), calculate the Euclidean distance:\n\n", sep = "")
  cat("```\n")
  cat("distance_to_cluster[i] = sqrt(sum((scaled_features - cluster_center[i])^2))\n")
  cat("```\n\n")
  cat("Where cluster_center[i] is the center of cluster i.\n\n")
  
  cat("**Step 4: Assign to Nearest Cluster**\n\n")
  cat("Assign the patient to the cluster with the minimum distance:\n\n")
  cat("```\n")
  cat("assigned_cluster = cluster with minimum distance\n")
  cat("```\n\n")
  
  cat("**Step 5: Map Cluster to Group Name**\n\n")
  cat("Use the following mapping to get the clinical group name:\n\n")
  
  cluster_mapping <- cluster_names %>%
    arrange(ml_cluster) %>%
    mutate(Cluster_Number = ml_cluster) %>%
    select(Cluster_Number, Clinical_Group_Name = group_name)
  
  kable(cluster_mapping, 
        caption = "Cluster Number to Clinical Group Name Mapping",
        col.names = c("Cluster Number", "Clinical Group Name")) %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
  
  cat("\n\n**Cluster Centers (for distance calculation):**\n\n")
  
  # Display cluster centers in a readable format
  cluster_centers_df <- as.data.frame(ml_model_parameters$cluster_centers)
  cluster_centers_df$Cluster <- 1:nrow(cluster_centers_df)
  cluster_centers_df <- cluster_centers_df %>%
    select(Cluster, everything()) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 4)))
  
  kable(cluster_centers_df, 
        caption = "Cluster Centers (Scaled Feature Values)",
        digits = 4) %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
    scroll_box(width = "100%", height = "400px")
  
  cat("\n\n**EXAMPLE CALCULATION:**\n\n")
  cat("1. Patient has 5 ctDNA measurements: [10.5, 8.2, 5.1, 2.3, 0.0]\n")
  cat("2. Calculate features:\n")
  cat("   - n_measurements = 5\n")
  cat("   - mean_ctdna = 5.22\n")
  cat("   - baseline_value = 10.5\n")
  cat("   - last_value = 0.0\n")
  cat("   - became_negative = 1 (started positive, ended negative)\n")
  cat("   - ... (calculate all features)\n")
  cat("3. Scale each feature using the Center and Scale values from the table above\n")
  cat("4. Calculate distance to each of the ", ml_model_parameters$n_clusters, " cluster centers\n", sep = "")
  cat("5. Assign to cluster with minimum distance\n")
  cat("6. Look up the Clinical Group Name from the mapping table\n\n")
  
  cat("**IMPORTANT NOTES:**\n")
  cat("- All features must be calculated exactly as described\n")
  cat("- Scaling must use the training set parameters (provided above)\n")
  cat("- Missing values should be set to 0\n")
  cat("- Infinite or NaN values should be set to 0\n")
  cat("- The model was trained on patients with ctDNA data only\n\n")
  
  # Export to CSV for easy use
  write.csv(scaling_params, "ML_Scaling_Parameters.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(cluster_centers_df, "ML_Cluster_Centers.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(cluster_mapping, "ML_Cluster_Names.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  
  cat("**Files Exported for Clinical Use:**\n")
  cat("- ML_Scaling_Parameters.csv: Feature scaling parameters\n")
  cat("- ML_Cluster_Centers.csv: Cluster center coordinates\n")
  cat("- ML_Cluster_Names.csv: Cluster to group name mapping\n")
  cat("- ML_Model_Specification.rds: Complete model specification (R format)\n\n")
  
} else {
  cat("ML model parameters not available. Please ensure the ML model has been trained.\n")
}
```

# ML-specific: Performance on train/validation/test sets
cat("\n=== ML Model: Train/Validation/Test Performance ===\n\n")

if (exists("ml_groups") && "dataset_split" %in% names(ml_groups)) {
  # Merge dataset_split info with survival data
  survival_ml_split <- survival_ml %>%
    left_join(ml_groups %>% select(patient_id, dataset_split), by = "patient_id") %>%
    filter(!is.na(dataset_split), !str_detect(tolower(ml_group), "no ctdna data"))
  
  # Calculate performance on each split
  ml_train_pfs <- calculate_c_index(survival_ml_split %>% filter(dataset_split == "Train"), 
                                     "pfs_time", "relapse_event", "ml_group")
  ml_val_pfs <- calculate_c_index(survival_ml_split %>% filter(dataset_split == "Validation"), 
                                   "pfs_time", "relapse_event", "ml_group")
  ml_test_pfs <- calculate_c_index(survival_ml_split %>% filter(dataset_split == "Test"), 
                                    "pfs_time", "relapse_event", "ml_group")
  
  ml_train_os <- calculate_c_index(survival_ml_split %>% filter(dataset_split == "Train"), 
                                    "os_time", "death_event", "ml_group")
  ml_val_os <- calculate_c_index(survival_ml_split %>% filter(dataset_split == "Validation"), 
                                  "os_time", "death_event", "ml_group")
  ml_test_os <- calculate_c_index(survival_ml_split %>% filter(dataset_split == "Test"), 
                                   "os_time", "death_event", "ml_group")
  
  ml_split_results <- tibble(
    Dataset = c("Train", "Validation", "Test"),
    PFS_C_Index = c(ml_train_pfs$c_index, ml_val_pfs$c_index, ml_test_pfs$c_index),
    PFS_N = c(ml_train_pfs$n, ml_val_pfs$n, ml_test_pfs$n),
    OS_C_Index = c(ml_train_os$c_index, ml_val_os$c_index, ml_test_os$c_index),
    OS_N = c(ml_train_os$n, ml_val_os$n, ml_test_os$n)
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      PFS_C_Index = round(PFS_C_Index, 3),
      OS_C_Index = round(OS_C_Index, 3)
    )
  
  cat("ML Model Performance by Dataset Split:\n")
  print(ml_split_results)
  
  cat("\nNote: Model was trained on training set only.\n")
  cat("Validation and test sets were assigned to nearest cluster centers from training model.\n")
  cat("Similar C-Index values across splits indicate good generalization.\n\n")
}

```{r comprehensive_patient_table}
# ==============================
# Comprehensive Patient Data Table
# ==============================

cat("\n=== Comprehensive Patient Data: ctDNA Levels and Clinical Outcomes ===\n\n")

# Create comprehensive table with ctDNA levels and outcomes
# Dataset should already be in survival_outcomes, but ensure it's there
comprehensive_table <- survival_outcomes %>%
  # Ensure dataset is present (it should be from all_patients)
  mutate(dataset = ifelse(is.na(dataset), "Unknown", dataset)) %>%
  # Add qualitative and quantitative groups
  left_join(qualitative_groups %>% select(patient_id, qualitative_group), by = "patient_id") %>%
  left_join(quantitative_groups %>% select(patient_id, quantitative_group), by = "patient_id") %>%
  left_join(ml_groups %>% select(patient_id, ml_group), by = "patient_id") %>%
  # Get all ctDNA measurements for each patient
  left_join(
    ctdna_long %>%
      group_by(patient_id) %>%
      summarise(
        ctDNA_measurements = paste(
          paste0(round(ctdna_value, 2), " (", format(ctdna_date, "%Y-%m-%d"), ")"),
          collapse = "; "
        ),
        n_ctDNA = n(),
        first_ctDNA_date = min(ctdna_date, na.rm = TRUE),
        last_ctDNA_date = max(ctdna_date, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = "patient_id"
  ) %>%
  # Select and arrange columns (only select columns that exist)
  select(
    patient_id,
    dataset,
    baseline_date,
    baseline_value,
    first_ctDNA_date,
    last_ctDNA_date,
    n_ctDNA,
    ctDNA_measurements,
    # Clinical outcomes
    relapse_date,
    relapse_event,
    time_to_relapse,
    survival_date,
    explicit_death_date,
    alive_yes_no,
    death_status_final,
    death_event,
    death_date,
    time_to_death,
    pfs_time,
    os_time,
    # Response categories
    qualitative_group,
    quantitative_group,
    ml_group
    # lbrecist_response  # Removed: LB-RECIST not needed
  ) %>%
  arrange(dataset, patient_id) %>%
  # Format dates for display
  mutate(
    baseline_date = format(baseline_date, "%Y-%m-%d"),
    first_ctDNA_date = format(first_ctDNA_date, "%Y-%m-%d"),
    last_ctDNA_date = format(last_ctDNA_date, "%Y-%m-%d"),
    relapse_date = ifelse(!is.na(relapse_date), format(relapse_date, "%Y-%m-%d"), NA_character_),
    survival_date = ifelse(!is.na(survival_date), format(survival_date, "%Y-%m-%d"), NA_character_),
    explicit_death_date = ifelse(!is.na(explicit_death_date), format(explicit_death_date, "%Y-%m-%d"), NA_character_),
    death_date = ifelse(!is.na(death_date), format(death_date, "%Y-%m-%d"), NA_character_),
    # Format numeric values
    baseline_value = round(baseline_value, 2),
    time_to_relapse = round(time_to_relapse, 1),
    time_to_death = round(time_to_death, 1),
    pfs_time = round(pfs_time, 1),
    os_time = round(os_time, 1),
    # Format event indicators
    relapse_event = ifelse(relapse_event == 1, "Yes", "No"),
    death_event = ifelse(death_event == 1, "Yes", "No"),
    death_status = case_when(
      death_status_final == 1 ~ "Dead",
      death_status_final == 0 ~ "Alive",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Rename columns for display
  rename(
    `Patient ID` = patient_id,
    `Dataset` = dataset,
    `Baseline Date` = baseline_date,
    `Baseline ctDNA` = baseline_value,
    `First ctDNA Date` = first_ctDNA_date,
    `Last ctDNA Date` = last_ctDNA_date,
    `# ctDNA Tests` = n_ctDNA,
    `ctDNA Measurements (value, date)` = ctDNA_measurements,
    `Relapse Date` = relapse_date,
    `Relapse Event` = relapse_event,
    `Time to Relapse (months)` = time_to_relapse,
    `Last Follow-up Date` = survival_date,
    `Explicit Death Date` = explicit_death_date,
    `Alive Yes/No` = alive_yes_no,
    `Death Status` = death_status,
    `Death Date` = death_date,
    `Death Event` = death_event,
    `Time to Death (months)` = time_to_death,
    `PFS Time (months)` = pfs_time,
    `OS Time (months)` = os_time,
    `Qualitative Group` = qualitative_group,
    `Quantitative Group` = quantitative_group,
    `ML Group` = ml_group
    # `LB-RECIST Response` = lbrecist_response  # Removed: LB-RECIST not needed
  )

# Display table with kable
kable(comprehensive_table, 
      caption = "Comprehensive Patient Data: ctDNA Levels and Clinical Outcomes",
      longtable = TRUE) %>%
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
    full_width = TRUE,
    font_size = 9,
    position = "left"
  ) %>%
  scroll_box(width = "100%", height = "600px")

cat("\n\nTotal patients in table:", nrow(comprehensive_table), "\n")
cat("Patients with relapse events:", sum(comprehensive_table$`Relapse Event` == "Yes", na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Patients with death events:", sum(comprehensive_table$`Death Event` == "Yes", na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

```{r asco_abstract}
# ==============================
# ASCO Abstract
# ==============================

cat("\n=== ASCO ABSTRACT ===\n\n")

# Get key statistics for abstract
if (exists("comparison_results") && exists("total_patients_abstract")) {
  
  # Extract best performing approach
  best_os_approach <- comparison_results$Approach[which.max(comparison_results$OS_C_Index)]
  best_os_cindex <- max(comparison_results$OS_C_Index, na.rm = TRUE)
  best_pfs_approach <- comparison_results$Approach[which.max(comparison_results$PFS_C_Index)]
  best_pfs_cindex <- max(comparison_results$PFS_C_Index, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Quantitative approach metrics
  quant_os_cindex <- comparison_results$OS_C_Index[comparison_results$Approach == "Quantitative"]
  quant_pfs_cindex <- comparison_results$PFS_C_Index[comparison_results$Approach == "Quantitative"]
  quant_os_n <- comparison_results$OS_N[comparison_results$Approach == "Quantitative"]
  quant_pfs_n <- comparison_results$PFS_N[comparison_results$Approach == "Quantitative"]
  
  cat("**TITLE:**\n")
  cat("Validation of Circulating Tumor DNA Response Criteria in Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer: A Retrospective Analysis Comparing Qualitative, Quantitative, and Machine Learning Approaches\n\n")
  
  cat("**BACKGROUND:**\n")
  cat("Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) has emerged as a promising predictive biomarker in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC), with potential applications in treatment response monitoring and prognostication. However, standardized and validated response criteria for ctDNA in this context are currently lacking, limiting its clinical utility. This study aimed to evaluate and validate various ctDNA response criteria in a retrospective cohort of MIBC patients to identify optimal criteria for clinical application.\n\n")
  
  cat("**METHODS:**\n")
  cat("We conducted a retrospective analysis of ", total_patients_abstract, " MIBC patients (Stage II or higher) from our institutional database. Three distinct ctDNA response criteria were applied to stratify patients:\n", sep = "")
  cat("(1) Qualitative approach: Categorization based on ctDNA positivity/negativity patterns (Clearance, Persistent Negative, Persistent Positive, Conversion);\n")
  cat("(2) Quantitative approach: Stratification based on percent change in ctDNA levels (Major Response ≥90% reduction, Partial Response ≥50% reduction, Stable, Progressive ≥50% increase);\n")
  cat("(3) Machine learning (ML) approach: K-means clustering incorporating multiple ctDNA features (baseline value, trend, variability, clearance/conversion patterns) to generate data-driven subgroups.\n")
  cat("The performance of each approach was evaluated using Harrell's Concordance Index (C-Index) for progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS), log-rank test p-values, and Akaike Information Criterion (AIC).\n\n")
  
  cat("**RESULTS:**\n")
  
  # Get actual values from comparison table
  qual_pfs_c <- comparison_results$PFS_C_Index[comparison_results$Approach == "Qualitative"]
  qual_os_c <- comparison_results$OS_C_Index[comparison_results$Approach == "Qualitative"]
  qual_pfs_n <- comparison_results$PFS_N[comparison_results$Approach == "Qualitative"]
  qual_os_n <- comparison_results$OS_N[comparison_results$Approach == "Qualitative"]
  
  ml_pfs_c <- comparison_results$PFS_C_Index[comparison_results$Approach == "ML"]
  ml_os_c <- comparison_results$OS_C_Index[comparison_results$Approach == "ML"]
  ml_pfs_n <- comparison_results$PFS_N[comparison_results$Approach == "ML"]
  ml_os_n <- comparison_results$OS_N[comparison_results$Approach == "ML"]
  
  # Check if Quantitative exists
  if ("Quantitative" %in% comparison_results$Approach) {
    quant_pfs_c <- comparison_results$PFS_C_Index[comparison_results$Approach == "Quantitative"]
    quant_os_c <- comparison_results$OS_C_Index[comparison_results$Approach == "Quantitative"]
    quant_pfs_n <- comparison_results$PFS_N[comparison_results$Approach == "Quantitative"]
    quant_os_n <- comparison_results$OS_N[comparison_results$Approach == "Quantitative"]
    
    # Determine best approach for each outcome
    best_os_approach <- comparison_results$Approach[which.max(comparison_results$OS_C_Index)]
    best_pfs_approach <- comparison_results$Approach[which.max(comparison_results$PFS_C_Index)]
    
    cat("Performance metrics for each approach are summarized in the table below. ")
    
    if (best_os_approach == "Quantitative") {
      cat("The quantitative approach demonstrated the highest discriminatory value for OS (C-Index = ", round(quant_os_c, 3), ", n = ", quant_os_n, "), ", sep = "")
      if (best_pfs_approach == "ML") {
        cat("followed by the ML approach (C-Index = ", round(ml_os_c, 3), ") and qualitative approach (C-Index = ", round(qual_os_c, 3), "). ", sep = "")
      } else {
        cat("followed by the qualitative approach (C-Index = ", round(qual_os_c, 3), ") and ML approach (C-Index = ", round(ml_os_c, 3), "). ", sep = "")
      }
      cat("For PFS, the ", best_pfs_approach, " approach showed the highest C-Index (", round(comparison_results$PFS_C_Index[comparison_results$Approach == best_pfs_approach], 3), ", n = ", comparison_results$PFS_N[comparison_results$Approach == best_pfs_approach], "). ", sep = "")
    } else if (best_os_approach == "ML") {
      cat("The ML approach demonstrated the highest discriminatory value for OS (C-Index = ", round(ml_os_c, 3), ", n = ", ml_os_n, "), ", sep = "")
      if ("Quantitative" %in% comparison_results$Approach) {
        cat("followed by the quantitative approach (C-Index = ", round(quant_os_c, 3), ") and qualitative approach (C-Index = ", round(qual_os_c, 3), "). ", sep = "")
      } else {
        cat("followed by the qualitative approach (C-Index = ", round(qual_os_c, 3), "). ", sep = "")
      }
      cat("For PFS, the ", best_pfs_approach, " approach showed the highest C-Index (", round(comparison_results$PFS_C_Index[comparison_results$Approach == best_pfs_approach], 3), ", n = ", comparison_results$PFS_N[comparison_results$Approach == best_pfs_approach], "). ", sep = "")
    } else {
      cat("The qualitative approach demonstrated OS C-Index of ", round(qual_os_c, 3), " (n = ", qual_os_n, "), ", sep = "")
      if ("Quantitative" %in% comparison_results$Approach) {
        cat("compared to quantitative (C-Index = ", round(quant_os_c, 3), ") and ML (C-Index = ", round(ml_os_c, 3), ") approaches. ", sep = "")
      } else {
        cat("compared to ML (C-Index = ", round(ml_os_c, 3), ") approach. ", sep = "")
      }
      cat("For PFS, the ", best_pfs_approach, " approach showed the highest C-Index (", round(comparison_results$PFS_C_Index[comparison_results$Approach == best_pfs_approach], 3), "). ", sep = "")
    }
    
    cat("All approaches showed highly significant log-rank test p-values (p < 0.001), indicating successful patient stratification.\n\n")
  } else {
    # Only Qualitative and ML available
    cat("Performance metrics for each approach are summarized in the table below. ")
    if (ml_os_c > qual_os_c) {
      cat("The ML approach demonstrated the highest discriminatory value for OS (C-Index = ", round(ml_os_c, 3), ", n = ", ml_os_n, "), compared to the qualitative approach (C-Index = ", round(qual_os_c, 3), ", n = ", qual_os_n, "). ", sep = "")
    } else {
      cat("The qualitative approach demonstrated OS C-Index of ", round(qual_os_c, 3), " (n = ", qual_os_n, "), compared to the ML approach (C-Index = ", round(ml_os_c, 3), ", n = ", ml_os_n, "). ", sep = "")
    }
    
    if (ml_pfs_c > qual_pfs_c) {
      cat("For PFS, the ML approach showed the highest C-Index (", round(ml_pfs_c, 3), ", n = ", ml_pfs_n, "), compared to the qualitative approach (C-Index = ", round(qual_pfs_c, 3), ", n = ", qual_pfs_n, "). ", sep = "")
    } else {
      cat("For PFS, the qualitative approach showed C-Index of ", round(qual_pfs_c, 3), " (n = ", qual_pfs_n, "), compared to the ML approach (C-Index = ", round(ml_pfs_c, 3), ", n = ", ml_pfs_n, "). ", sep = "")
    }
    cat("All approaches showed highly significant log-rank test p-values (p < 0.001), indicating successful patient stratification.\n\n")
  }
  
  # Create results table for abstract
  abstract_table <- comparison_results %>%
    mutate(
      PFS_LogRank_P_Formatted = ifelse(PFS_LogRank_P < 0.001, "<0.001", as.character(round(PFS_LogRank_P, 3))),
      OS_LogRank_P_Formatted = ifelse(OS_LogRank_P < 0.001, "<0.001", as.character(round(OS_LogRank_P, 3)))
    ) %>%
    select(Approach, PFS_C_Index, PFS_LogRank_P_Formatted, PFS_N, OS_C_Index, OS_LogRank_P_Formatted, OS_N)
  
  kable(abstract_table,
        caption = "Performance Comparison of ctDNA Response Criteria",
        col.names = c("Approach", "PFS C-Index", "PFS Log-Rank P", "PFS N", 
                     "OS C-Index", "OS Log-Rank P", "OS N"),
        digits = 3) %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
  
  cat("\n**CONCLUSIONS:**\n")
  
  # Determine best overall OS approach for conclusions
  if ("Quantitative" %in% comparison_results$Approach) {
    best_overall_os <- comparison_results$Approach[which.max(comparison_results$OS_C_Index)]
    best_os_cindex_val <- max(comparison_results$OS_C_Index, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    if (best_overall_os == "Quantitative") {
      cat("Among the evaluated approaches, the quantitative ctDNA response criteria demonstrated the highest discriminatory value, particularly for overall survival (C-Index = ", round(best_os_cindex_val, 3), "). The quantitative approach, which stratifies patients based on percent change in ctDNA levels, provides a clinically interpretable and robust method for assessing treatment response. These findings suggest that quantitative assessment of ctDNA dynamics may serve as a valuable prognostic tool in MIBC. Prospective validation of these criteria in larger, multi-institutional cohorts is warranted to establish standardized ctDNA response metrics for clinical practice and to confirm their utility in guiding treatment decisions.\n\n", sep = "")
    } else if (best_overall_os == "ML") {
      cat("Among the evaluated approaches, the machine learning-based ctDNA response criteria demonstrated the highest discriminatory value for overall survival (C-Index = ", round(best_os_cindex_val, 3), "), followed by the quantitative approach (C-Index = ", round(quant_os_cindex, 3), "). The ML approach, which incorporates multiple ctDNA features to generate data-driven subgroups, and the quantitative approach, which stratifies patients based on percent change in ctDNA levels, both provide valuable methods for assessing treatment response. These findings suggest that both quantitative and ML-based assessment of ctDNA dynamics may serve as valuable prognostic tools in MIBC. Prospective validation of these criteria, particularly the quantitative approach given its clinical interpretability, in larger, multi-institutional cohorts is warranted to establish standardized ctDNA response metrics for clinical practice.\n\n", sep = "")
    } else {
      cat("Among the evaluated approaches, the quantitative ctDNA response criteria demonstrated the highest discriminatory value for overall survival (C-Index = ", round(quant_os_cindex, 3), "), compared to qualitative (C-Index = ", round(qual_os_c, 3), ") and ML (C-Index = ", round(ml_os_c, 3), ") approaches. The quantitative approach, which stratifies patients based on percent change in ctDNA levels, provides a clinically interpretable and robust method for assessing treatment response. These findings suggest that quantitative assessment of ctDNA dynamics may serve as a valuable prognostic tool in MIBC. Prospective validation of these criteria in larger, multi-institutional cohorts is warranted to establish standardized ctDNA response metrics for clinical practice.\n\n", sep = "")
    }
  } else {
    # Only Qualitative and ML
    best_overall_os <- if (ml_os_c > qual_os_c) "ML" else "Qualitative"
    best_os_cindex_val <- max(ml_os_c, qual_os_c)
    
    if (best_overall_os == "ML") {
      cat("Among the evaluated approaches, the machine learning-based ctDNA response criteria demonstrated the highest discriminatory value for overall survival (C-Index = ", round(ml_os_c, 3), "), compared to the qualitative approach (C-Index = ", round(qual_os_c, 3), "). The ML approach, which incorporates multiple ctDNA features to generate data-driven subgroups, provides a robust method for assessing treatment response. For PFS, the ML approach also showed superior discrimination (C-Index = ", round(ml_pfs_c, 3), ") compared to the qualitative approach (C-Index = ", round(qual_pfs_c, 3), "). These findings suggest that ML-based assessment of ctDNA dynamics may serve as a valuable prognostic tool in MIBC. Prospective validation of these criteria in larger, multi-institutional cohorts is warranted to establish standardized ctDNA response metrics for clinical practice.\n\n", sep = "")
    } else {
      cat("Among the evaluated approaches, both qualitative and ML-based ctDNA response criteria demonstrated similar discriminatory value for overall survival (Qualitative C-Index = ", round(qual_os_c, 3), "; ML C-Index = ", round(ml_os_c, 3), "). For PFS, the ML approach showed superior discrimination (C-Index = ", round(ml_pfs_c, 3), ") compared to the qualitative approach (C-Index = ", round(qual_pfs_c, 3), "). Both approaches successfully stratify patients based on ctDNA patterns, with the ML approach showing particular promise for PFS prediction. Prospective validation of these criteria in larger, multi-institutional cohorts is warranted to establish standardized ctDNA response metrics for clinical practice.\n\n", sep = "")
    }
  }
  
  cat("**KEY WORDS:**\n")
  cat("Circulating tumor DNA, ctDNA, muscle-invasive bladder cancer, response criteria, biomarkers, survival analysis\n\n")
  
  # Determine best overall OS approach for conclusions
  if ("Quantitative" %in% comparison_results$Approach) {
    best_overall_os <- comparison_results$Approach[which.max(comparison_results$OS_C_Index)]
    best_os_cindex_val <- max(comparison_results$OS_C_Index, na.rm = TRUE)
  } else {
    best_overall_os <- if (ml_os_c > qual_os_c) "ML" else "Qualitative"
    best_os_cindex_val <- max(ml_os_c, qual_os_c)
  }
  
  # Export abstract to text file
  results_text <- if ("Quantitative" %in% comparison_results$Approach) {
    paste0("Performance metrics for each approach are summarized in the table. ", 
           if (best_os_approach == "Quantitative") {
             paste0("The quantitative approach demonstrated the highest discriminatory value for OS (C-Index = ", round(quant_os_cindex, 3), ", n = ", quant_os_n, "), followed by the ML approach (C-Index = ", round(ml_os_c, 3), ") and qualitative approach (C-Index = ", round(qual_os_c, 3), "). ")
           } else if (best_os_approach == "ML") {
             paste0("The ML approach demonstrated the highest discriminatory value for OS (C-Index = ", round(ml_os_c, 3), ", n = ", ml_os_n, "), followed by the quantitative approach (C-Index = ", round(quant_os_cindex, 3), ") and qualitative approach (C-Index = ", round(qual_os_c, 3), "). ")
           } else {
             paste0("The qualitative approach demonstrated OS C-Index of ", round(qual_os_c, 3), " (n = ", qual_os_n, "), compared to quantitative (C-Index = ", round(quant_os_cindex, 3), ") and ML (C-Index = ", round(ml_os_c, 3), ") approaches. ")
           },
           "For PFS, the ", best_pfs_approach, " approach showed the highest C-Index (", round(comparison_results$PFS_C_Index[comparison_results$Approach == best_pfs_approach], 3), ", n = ", comparison_results$PFS_N[comparison_results$Approach == best_pfs_approach], "). All approaches showed highly significant log-rank test p-values (p < 0.001), indicating successful patient stratification.\n\n")
  } else {
    paste0("Performance metrics for each approach are summarized in the table. ",
           if (ml_os_c > qual_os_c) {
             paste0("The ML approach demonstrated the highest discriminatory value for OS (C-Index = ", round(ml_os_c, 3), ", n = ", ml_os_n, "), compared to the qualitative approach (C-Index = ", round(qual_os_c, 3), ", n = ", qual_os_n, "). ")
           } else {
             paste0("The qualitative approach demonstrated OS C-Index of ", round(qual_os_c, 3), " (n = ", qual_os_n, "), compared to the ML approach (C-Index = ", round(ml_os_c, 3), ", n = ", ml_os_n, "). ")
           },
           if (ml_pfs_c > qual_pfs_c) {
             paste0("For PFS, the ML approach showed the highest C-Index (", round(ml_pfs_c, 3), ", n = ", ml_pfs_n, "), compared to the qualitative approach (C-Index = ", round(qual_pfs_c, 3), ", n = ", qual_pfs_n, "). ")
           } else {
             paste0("For PFS, the qualitative approach showed C-Index of ", round(qual_pfs_c, 3), " (n = ", qual_pfs_n, "), compared to the ML approach (C-Index = ", round(ml_pfs_c, 3), ", n = ", ml_pfs_n, "). ")
           },
           "All approaches showed highly significant log-rank test p-values (p < 0.001), indicating successful patient stratification.\n\n")
  }
  
  conclusions_text <- if ("Quantitative" %in% comparison_results$Approach) {
    if (best_overall_os == "Quantitative") {
      paste0("Among the evaluated approaches, the quantitative ctDNA response criteria demonstrated the highest discriminatory value, particularly for overall survival (C-Index = ", round(best_os_cindex_val, 3), "). The quantitative approach, which stratifies patients based on percent change in ctDNA levels, provides a clinically interpretable and robust method for assessing treatment response. These findings suggest that quantitative assessment of ctDNA dynamics may serve as a valuable prognostic tool in MIBC. Prospective validation of these criteria in larger, multi-institutional cohorts is warranted to establish standardized ctDNA response metrics for clinical practice and to confirm their utility in guiding treatment decisions.\n")
    } else if (best_overall_os == "ML") {
      paste0("Among the evaluated approaches, the machine learning-based ctDNA response criteria demonstrated the highest discriminatory value for overall survival (C-Index = ", round(best_os_cindex_val, 3), "), followed by the quantitative approach (C-Index = ", round(quant_os_cindex, 3), "). The ML approach, which incorporates multiple ctDNA features to generate data-driven subgroups, and the quantitative approach, which stratifies patients based on percent change in ctDNA levels, both provide valuable methods for assessing treatment response. These findings suggest that both quantitative and ML-based assessment of ctDNA dynamics may serve as valuable prognostic tools in MIBC. Prospective validation of these criteria, particularly the quantitative approach given its clinical interpretability, in larger, multi-institutional cohorts is warranted to establish standardized ctDNA response metrics for clinical practice.\n")
    } else {
      paste0("Among the evaluated approaches, the quantitative ctDNA response criteria demonstrated the highest discriminatory value for overall survival (C-Index = ", round(quant_os_cindex, 3), "), compared to qualitative (C-Index = ", round(qual_os_c, 3), ") and ML (C-Index = ", round(ml_os_c, 3), ") approaches. The quantitative approach, which stratifies patients based on percent change in ctDNA levels, provides a clinically interpretable and robust method for assessing treatment response. These findings suggest that quantitative assessment of ctDNA dynamics may serve as a valuable prognostic tool in MIBC. Prospective validation of these criteria in larger, multi-institutional cohorts is warranted to establish standardized ctDNA response metrics for clinical practice.\n")
    }
  } else {
    if (best_overall_os == "ML") {
      paste0("Among the evaluated approaches, the machine learning-based ctDNA response criteria demonstrated the highest discriminatory value for overall survival (C-Index = ", round(ml_os_c, 3), "), compared to the qualitative approach (C-Index = ", round(qual_os_c, 3), "). The ML approach, which incorporates multiple ctDNA features to generate data-driven subgroups, provides a robust method for assessing treatment response. For PFS, the ML approach also showed superior discrimination (C-Index = ", round(ml_pfs_c, 3), ") compared to the qualitative approach (C-Index = ", round(qual_pfs_c, 3), "). These findings suggest that ML-based assessment of ctDNA dynamics may serve as a valuable prognostic tool in MIBC. Prospective validation of these criteria in larger, multi-institutional cohorts is warranted to establish standardized ctDNA response metrics for clinical practice.\n")
    } else {
      paste0("Among the evaluated approaches, both qualitative and ML-based ctDNA response criteria demonstrated similar discriminatory value for overall survival (Qualitative C-Index = ", round(qual_os_c, 3), "; ML C-Index = ", round(ml_os_c, 3), "). For PFS, the ML approach showed superior discrimination (C-Index = ", round(ml_pfs_c, 3), ") compared to the qualitative approach (C-Index = ", round(qual_pfs_c, 3), "). Both approaches successfully stratify patients based on ctDNA patterns, with the ML approach showing particular promise for PFS prediction. Prospective validation of these criteria in larger, multi-institutional cohorts is warranted to establish standardized ctDNA response metrics for clinical practice.\n")
    }
  }
  
  abstract_text <- paste0(
    "TITLE:\n",
    "Validation of Circulating Tumor DNA Response Criteria in Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer: A Retrospective Analysis Comparing Qualitative, Quantitative, and Machine Learning Approaches\n\n",
    "BACKGROUND:\n",
    "Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) has emerged as a promising predictive biomarker in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC), with potential applications in treatment response monitoring and prognostication. However, standardized and validated response criteria for ctDNA in this context are currently lacking, limiting its clinical utility. This study aimed to evaluate and validate various ctDNA response criteria in a retrospective cohort of MIBC patients to identify optimal criteria for clinical application.\n\n",
    "METHODS:\n",
    "We conducted a retrospective analysis of ", total_patients_abstract, " MIBC patients (Stage II or higher) from our institutional database. Three distinct ctDNA response criteria were applied to stratify patients: (1) Qualitative approach: Categorization based on ctDNA positivity/negativity patterns (Clearance, Persistent Negative, Persistent Positive, Conversion); (2) Quantitative approach: Stratification based on percent change in ctDNA levels (Major Response ≥90% reduction, Partial Response ≥50% reduction, Stable, Progressive ≥50% increase); (3) Machine learning (ML) approach: K-means clustering incorporating multiple ctDNA features (baseline value, trend, variability, clearance/conversion patterns) to generate data-driven subgroups. The performance of each approach was evaluated using Harrell's Concordance Index (C-Index) for progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS), log-rank test p-values, and Akaike Information Criterion (AIC).\n\n",
    "RESULTS:\n",
    results_text,
    "CONCLUSIONS:\n",
    conclusions_text
  )
  
  writeLines(abstract_text, "ASCO_Abstract.txt")
  cat("Abstract exported to: ASCO_Abstract.txt\n")
  
} else {
  cat("Comparison results not available. Please ensure the analysis has been completed.\n")
}
